about_text: I´m passionate about equity, diversity, & inclusion. I guide and support business leaders to embed DE&I as part of the business agenda and priorities.As a savvy and dynamic leader, I combine my experience and expertise in DE&I, marketing, and customer strategy for sustainable implementation, continuous improvement, and development. I focus on targeted change management and scalable solutions for organizational transformation. Throughout role-modeling vulnerable leadership, I have worked with global leadership teams, to empower creativity and innovation. I have extensive experience in project and stakeholder management, awareness campaign design, and execution. Prior to my current role in DE&I, I was focused on defining sales and marketing strategies, as well as the design and adoption of CRM systems, the voice of the customer, market trends, and KPI analysis. I represent corporate diversity in multiple dimensions, which allows me to understand different types of cultures, business models, and ways of working. I hold two master's degrees, and over 15 years of experience in global corporations from various industries such as automotive, financial services, and life science.Born in Mexico, and living in Switzerland, I am a proud member of the LGBTQI+ community and currently leading the ED&I strategy as Group Head of Diversity and Inclusion for the Syngenta Group and its 50,000 people across more than 100 countries.I am highly driven to create an inclusive and equitable environment for the diverse team in the Syngenta Group by focusing on fostering and promoting psychological safety, mental health, equal payment for equal jobs, and zero tolerance for racist and harassing behaviors. I am a firm believer that everyone in the organization should embrace equity, diversity, and inclusion, since it will help keep the business thriving, and is the right thing to do.

About: Waldo helps leaders & teams adapt to massive change and grow collaborative cultures of courage, resilience and mutual support. A New York Times and Wall Street Journal bestselling author and Hall of Fame speaker, he delivers keynotes and seminars (live/virtual), executive coaching, and sales & leadership programs to small entrepreneurial firms to the largest companies in the world. An expert on change management, peak performance & resilience, Waldo works with entrepreneurs, sales teams, managers & executives to help them break performance barriers, overcome obstacles & build cultures of collaboration, courage, and trust. Known as "The Wingman," he’s an Air Force Academy graduate, MBA, combat decorated Air Force F-16 fighter pilot turned sales manager, performance consultant, executive coach and motivational keynote speaker. Waldo’s philosophy: No fighter pilot flies solo and neither should you. Clients include Siemens, American Express, Home Depot, Oppenheimer, Dell, Deloitte, Verizon, Merck, The Denver Broncos, New York Life, Hewlett Packard, Caterpillar, and dozens of national associations. About: RaJade M. Berry-James, Ph.D., is senior associate dean of faculty and academic affairs at the L. Douglas Wilder School of Government and Public Affairs at VCU in Richmond VA. Elected Vice President and President-Elect of Network of Schools of Public Policy, Affairs, and Administration (NASPAA). Elected Fellow of the  National Academy of Public Administration (NAPA) and Vice Chair of the Standing  Panel on Social Equity in Governance. She has spent 30+ years in higher education as Chair of the Faculty; Director of Graduate Programs, MPA Program Coordinator, PhD Program Coordinator directing small, large & research-intensive graduate programs; Assistant to the Dean for School of Liberal Arts, Assistant then Associate Director of Institutional Research. She is a consultant, specializing in diversity, equity & inclusion as well as higher education assessment and accreditation.Jade's research, teaching & service focus on theory of change and applied practice of public administration. Her book Why Research Methods  Matter: Essential Skills in Decision Making (2018), examines real-world policymaking and evidence to support decision-making. Jade designed NASPAA award-winning courses, MPA Capstone and Cultural Competence in the Public Sector, and has taught graduate courses in Basic Quantitative Research, Advanced Research, and Statistical Methods, Research Methods and Analysis, Public Policymaking, Implementation and Evaluation, Survey Research, Program Evaluation, Public Bureaucracy, Personnel Management, Conflict Resolution, and Social Equity. Her research is published in PAR, JPAE, ROPPA, PPMR, International Journal of Public  Administration, Int'l Association for the Study of Global Achievement of Gap, Int'l Journal of the Humanities, Public Budgeting, Accounting and Financial  Management, Black Political Research, American Society of Professional Emergency Planners,  and Public Management & Social Policy (JPMSP). Her evaluation research was funded by W. K. Kellogg Foundation,  U.S. Dept of Health and Human Services, SAMHSA/Center for Substance Abuse Treatment (CSAT) & Center for Substance Abuse Prevention (CSAP), U.S. Office of Juvenile Justice and Delinquency Prevention, Office of National Drug Control Policy (ONDCP), OH Dept of Alcohol and Drug Addiction Services (ODADAS), Summit County (OH) Juvenile Court, Summit County (OH) Dept of Jobs & Family Services, and Akron Center for Policy Studies; she served on ASPA National Council, NASPAA Executive Council, and Chair of COPRA. Her work is guided by an old Ethiopian proverb, "S/he who learns, teaches."

Data from the U.S. Census is fundamental to apportioning political power as well as more than $800 billion each year for governmental services. In each state, population totals will determine the House of Representative seats. These undercounts pose on‐going challenges to political participation, representation, and resources. Implementation of Census 2020 is the responsibility of public administrators, and there are important challenges relative to civil rights and social equity.

About: RaJade M. Berry-James, Ph.D., is senior associate dean of faculty and academic affairs at the L. Douglas Wilder School of Government and Public Affairs at VCU in Richmond VA. Elected Vice President and President-Elect of Network of Schools of Public Policy, Affairs, and Administration (NASPAA). Elected Fellow of the National Academy of Public Administration (NAPA) and Vice Chair of the Standing Panel on Social Equity in Governance. She has spent 30+ years in higher education as Chair of the Faculty; Director of Graduate Programs, MPA Program Coordinator, PhD Program Coordinator directing small, large & research-intensive graduate programs; Assistant to the Dean for School of Liberal Arts, Assistant then Associate Director of Institutional Research. She is a consultant, specializing in diversity, equity & inclusion as well as higher education assessment and accreditation.Jade's research, teaching & service focus on theory of change and applied practice of public administration. Her book Why Research Methods Matter: Essential Skills in Decision Making (2018), examines real-world policymaking and evidence to support decision-making. Jade designed NASPAA award-winning courses, MPA Capstone and Cultural Competence in the Public Sector, and has taught graduate courses in Basic Quantitative Research, Advanced Research, and Statistical Methods, Research Methods and Analysis, Public Policymaking, Implementation and Evaluation, Survey Research, Program Evaluation, Public Bureaucracy, Personnel Management, Conflict Resolution, and Social Equity. Her research is published in PAR, JPAE, ROPPA, PPMR, International Journal of Public Administration, Int'l Association for the Study of Global Achievement of Gap, Int'l Journal of the Humanities, Public Budgeting, Accounting and Financial Management, Black Political Research, American Society of Professional Emergency Planners, and Public Management & Social Policy (JPMSP). Her evaluation research was funded by W. K. Kellogg Foundation, U.S. Dept of Health and Human Services, SAMHSA/Center for Substance Abuse Treatment (CSAT) & Center for Substance Abuse Prevention (CSAP), U.S. Office of Juvenile Justice and Delinquency Prevention, Office of National Drug Control Policy (ONDCP), OH Dept of Alcohol and Drug Addiction Services (ODADAS), Summit County (OH) Juvenile Court, Summit County (OH) Dept of Jobs & Family Services, and Akron Center for Policy Studies; she served on ASPA National Council, NASPAA Executive Council, and Chair of COPRA. Her work is guided by an old Ethiopian proverb, "S/he who learns, teaches."

About: I am Associate Professor of Neurology at Northwestern University, Feinberg School of Medicine.I am also a faculty member at the Les Turner ALS Center, the Mesulam Cognitive Neurology and Alzheimer's Disease Center and the Robert H. Lurie Comprehensive Cancer Center.We are interested in understanding the molecular and cellular basis of neuronal vulnerability that is observed in distinct neuron populations in different diseases. We focus our attention to the upper motor neurons that die in ALS, HSP and PLS. However, we have a broad interest in the common cellular mechanisms that lead to neuronal degeneration. We generated and characterized the first reporter line for upper motor neurons and developed a novel drug discovery/verification platform that incorporates improved upper motor neuron health as a readout. Interestingly, even for the diseases that have been characterized by the loss of upper motor neurons, their health has never been considered for any of the preclinical assays. In addition to being a scientist, I am a painter, a writer, an international press member, a mother and an advocate for women, science and education. Assent would like to thank all participants in the room, who came from a wide range of industrial sectors for the excellent interactive discussion which took place. | Publication: 1: 1: Title: Automation in military operations | 1: Journal: UK Parliamentary Office of Science and Technology. · Oct 7, 2022 | 1: Description: Contributor & Reviewer | Publication: 2: 2: Title: Navigating Supply Chain Multiverses: The colliding worlds of ESG and Product Compliance Reporting, implications for reporting across global supply chains | 2: Journal: American Chemistry Society, Green Chemistry Institute: 26th Annual Green Chemistry & Engineering Conference. · Jun 8, 2022 | 2: Description: Companies that place products onto the marketplace, whether they are internally manufactured or sourced from a supply chain face ever increasing requirements to provision data, wherever the products are sourced and transported from, manufactured, and distributed at applicable local, regional, and global levels.The Product Compliance world considers product safety and regulatory compliance activities. The Environmental, Social, and corporate Governance (ESG) world considers a much broader range of sustainability and social development related activities, performed at a corporate level. ESG reporting was originally developed within the financial sector by investors to aggregate a given organization reporting against ESG related topics.The European Union (EU) has been implementing additional EU ESG reporting requirements, in the form of several directives and regulations flowing down from the EU Green Deal, which aligns all it’s actions against the EU 2030 Climate Target Plan, this includes EU Capital Markets Action Plan, which includes direct intervention in the financial sector, requiring EU financial sector to adhere to the new EU ESG reporting requirements when providing financial services to industry. As a result, companies within the EU will need to adhere to these new EU ESG reporting requirements, which include reporting at economic activity and product level, to obtain investment from the EU financial sector, hence a significant additional burden of reporting will be placed against global supply chains in a significantly different manner to traditional ESG reporting, resulting in the collection of data and reporting linked to economic activities and at the product level, fusing the worlds of Product Compliance and ESG reporting. Existing systems and standards will need to be updated to reflect the granularity and accuracy of data to be reported.

We are in the midsts of two major crises in America: mental health and race-relations. They impact our homes, schools, businesses, relationships, and (obviously) sanity — but do we recognize the signs of these problems? Are we doing enough on the front-end to prevent personal and professional disasters from happening? As a keynote speaker, consultant, and workshop facilitator, Doyin provides tangible, actionable solutions that provides results for his clients all over America. Doyin’s newest book, WATCH ME details the immigration story of his dad who came to the states from a so-called “shithole country” (don’t worry, that language isn’t in the book) to secure his Ph.D. from one of the top universities in the country while adding immense value to America in the process. about_text: Doyin Richards is a dynamic keynote speaker who inspires men to be open about mental health, embrace anti-racism, and be the best dads/parenting partners they can be. We are in the midsts of two major crises in America: mental health and race-relations. They impact our homes, schools, businesses, relationships, and (obviously) sanity — but do we recognize the signs of these problems? Are we doing enough on the front-end to prevent personal and professional disasters from happening? As a keynote speaker, consultant, and workshop facilitator, Doyin provides tangible, actionable solutions that provides results for his clients all over America. Cisco, Amgen, Salesforce, LexisNexis, PwC, and Marvell are a few of the companies where he recently delivered a keynote address. Mainstream media values his message as he's often called on to make appearances for NPR and HLN, and has been interviewed by the TODAY Show, ABC News, Essence Magazine, Cosmopolitan, USA Today, CNN, Parents Magazine, Yahoo!, T.D. Jakes, the New York Times, Sunrise Australia, and more. His message isn't just for adults. Doyin authored two picture books for children published by Feiwel & Friends (an imprint of mega-publisher Macmillan). The first was I WONDER that recognizes the insecurities many new fathers have while raising their children, but also celebrates the fact that dads are never insecure when it comes to the love they have for their kiddos. His next picture book, WHAT'S THE DIFFERENCE? tackles the tough topic of introducing kids to positive race-relations without raising them to be "colorblind." It was the #1 New Release in the ultra-competitive children's "Explore The World" category on Amazon. Doyin’s newest book, WATCH ME details the immigration story of his dad who came to the states from a so-called “shithole country” (don’t worry, that language isn’t in the book) to secure his Ph.D. from one of the top universities in the country while adding immense value to America in the process. Through his books, keynote speeches, workshops, media appearances, and his new Anti-Racism Fight Club virtual seminar, Doyin regularly demonstrates that he is a leader in the fields of mental health, anti-racism, healthy masculinity, and fatherhood.

About: As Executive Vice President and Chief Diversity Officer of Comcast Corporation and President of the Comcast NBCUniversal Foundation, I oversee all Diversity, Equity, & Inclusion initiatives and philanthropic strategy for the corporation with a focus on advancing digital equity through Project UP, and the company’s $100 million pledge to advance social justice and equality. I also lead Comcast’s community impact initiatives, working across the organization to provide strategic leadership for all corporate social responsibility programs, including employee engagement and volunteerism. I currently serve on the boards of United Way of Greater Philadelphia and Southern NJ, Kimmel Center for the Performing Arts, and OceanFirst Bank. And I have had the honor of being named one of the “Most Powerful Women in Cable” by Cablefax Magazine, one of the “Most Powerful Women in Business” by Black Enterprise, and an “Innovative Rising Star: Building Communities” by Forbes magazine. Most recently, I received the inaugural “Wave Maker” Award; was recognized by ColorComm as one of the "28 Black Women in Communications Making History Now;” and named a “2022 Wonder Woman” by Multichannel News.

about_text: As a young educator, graphic design, visual arts, technology has always been a great passion of mine. With more than eight years of teaching experience, I have found a way to effectively incorporate esports educational advancements in both K-12 and collegiate settings. Living by the motto that esports is an effective way to promote student engagement across the curriculum, I have excelled at becoming an advocate for esports through curriculum development, coaching, and consulting. Since becoming a certified K-12 Esports Provider and certified Esports Club Sponsor through the Esports Education Network and establishing the Geaux Play Esports podcast, I have set out on a mission to enrich the lives of all educators, gamers, and students. I aspire to improve and transform the way in which educators view esports, align curriculum standards, obtain funding, and build long lasting esports clubs and programs.

Workplace: Chief Financial Officer at Raymond James Financial, Inc.
About: Paul Shoukry is chief financial officer of Raymond James Financial, Inc. (NYSE: RJF). He is responsible for the overall financial management of the company, including balance sheet management, financial reporting, investor relations, corporate development, corporate tax, cash management, regulatory reporting and financial planning and analysis. Mr. Shoukry also oversees the company’s ESG strategy, initiatives and reporting. He is a member of the firm’s Executive Committee and serves on the boards of subsidiaries Raymond James & Associates and TriState Capital Bank.  Mr. Shoukry joined Raymond James in 2010 to participate in the firm's Assistant to the Chairman program. He earned an MBA with honors from Columbia University. Before business school, Mr. Shoukry worked for a strategy consulting firm that focused on serving clients in the financial services industry. He started his career as a commercial banker after graduating magna cum laude with a Bachelor and Master of Accounting from The University of Georgia. Mr. Shoukry also completed the Strategic CFO Program at The Wharton School. He is a Certified Public Accountant (CPA), a Certified Treasury Professional, and a Series 7 and 27 holder. Mr. Shoukry was named to Fortune's "40 under 40 in Finance." Mr. Shoukry enjoys golfing and spending time with his wife and three children. He is passionate about childhood education and serves on the board of trustees for Academy Prep Center of Tampa. About: Holly O’Neill is President of Retail Banking, one of Bank of America’s eight lines of business, and a member of the company’s executive management team.Holly is responsible for the growth of the business that serves 33 million U.S. mass market consumers with a full range of financial products and services through award-winning digital banking capabilities and an unmatched retail banking network.She previously led Client Care and Client Experience, which are now part of the Retail Banking organization and tasked with providing financial solutions to the bank’s clients while delivering an exceptional and distinctive experience.Holly also served as Chief Operating Officer for Bank of America Private Bank overseeing strategic initiatives, business management, risk infrastructure and control, enterprise partnerships, and sales and service effectiveness. She also served as the COO for Merrill Lynch Wealth Management® Private Banking and Investment Group.She joined Bank of America in 1996 as a credit analyst in the Corporate and Investment Bank where she held various roles, including corporate banker covering a portfolio of insurance and asset management clients and as COO of the Corporate Banking Group.Holly is active in enterprise-wide efforts as an executive sponsor leading awareness and inclusion strategies for the LGBTQ+ community, individuals with disabilities and women.She holds a Bachelor of Science degree in business from the University of New Hampshire and lives in Marblehead, Massachusetts, with her husband and three children.If you are interested in a career at Bank of America, please visit: https://careers.bankofamerica.com/en-us

About: Holly O’Neill is President of Retail Banking, one of Bank of America’s eight lines of business, and a member of the company’s executive management team.Holly is responsible for the growth of the business that serves 33 million U.S. mass market consumers with a full range of financial products and services through award-winning digital banking capabilities and an unmatched retail banking network.She previously led Client Care and Client Experience, which are now part of the Retail Banking organization and tasked with providing financial solutions to the bank’s clients while delivering an exceptional and distinctive experience.Holly also served as Chief Operating Officer for Bank of America Private Bank overseeing strategic initiatives, business management, risk infrastructure and control, enterprise partnerships, and sales and service effectiveness. She also served as the COO for Merrill Lynch Wealth Management® Private Banking and Investment Group.She joined Bank of America in 1996 as a credit analyst in the Corporate and Investment Bank where she held various roles, including corporate banker covering a portfolio of insurance and asset management clients and as COO of the Corporate Banking Group.Holly is active in enterprise-wide efforts as an executive sponsor leading awareness and inclusion strategies for the LGBTQ+ community, individuals with disabilities and women.She holds a Bachelor of Science degree in business from the University of New Hampshire and lives in Marblehead, Massachusetts, with her husband and three children.If you are interested in a career at Bank of America, please visit: https://careers.bankofamerica.com/en-us

I joined Bank of America in 1996 as a credit analyst trainee. about_text: I am a Chicago native and world enthusiast who is deeply passionate about creating healthy and thriving communities through servant leadership, volunteerism, community engagement and paying it forward. My personal passion for community and service has aligned with my professional journey in business development, client relationship management, corporate philanthropy, corporate social responsibility, diversity, equity & inclusion. I have a diverse banking career in areas such as wealth management, commercial lending and community giving. I thrive in organizations with opportunity to build programs and strategies to deliver outcomes aligned to business priorities. Developing and deepening strong, sustainable relationships with various stakeholders such as clients, internal and external partners, senior and executive leadership and communities are critical to my success. I currently serve as Executive Vice President, Chief Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Officer for Old National Bank, responsible for developing and implementing an integrated business informed strategy across 7 states serving over 4,200 employees. Responsibilities include driving and integrating robust diversity, equity and inclusion programs into business practices and processes to build inclusive leadership capabilities and promote diversity at all levels of the enterprise. Working closely with the board of directors, C- suite executives and senior leadership, I ensure diversity, inclusion and corporate social responsibility are strategically driving business performance, investing in our colleagues, clients and communities, and building a stronger company to meet the needs of current stakeholders and future generations.

About: Brenda Christensen is CEO of Stellar Public Relations, a world leader in public relations, investor relations, branding, funding and corporate guidance with direct attributable growth worth over millions of dollars. Ms. Christensen currently serves as an adviser on private boards in North America, and previously served as corporate officer for a publicly held technology company, across multiple continents.A leading corporate communications and public relations expert, board member and corporate officer of top global technology companies, Brenda has provided strategic corporate guidance and governance, as well as successfully created and managed global messaging campaigns for such prestigious companies as Tinder, Apple, McAfee, Panda Security, NEC, GM and others.In March 2020, she was named "Top 15 in Security PR" by noted author and cybersecurity thought leader, Richard Stiennon, voted “PR SourceCode Top 10 Tech Communicators” by 800 leading journalists and bloggers, as well as “Best PR in Tech” by Robert Scoble. In addition, she is listed as a top PR pro to follow on Twitter by Business2Community and HubSpot named her one of the “Most Influential on Facebook." Ms. Christensen was selected by The Economist for its prestigious cybersecurity simulation panel, including Richard A. Clarke, chief counter-terrorism advisor under George W. Bush for the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks (https://www.dailymotion.com/video/x6fblpu).As PR Director for Secure Computing, she orchestrated a successful post-acquisition restructuring of global public relations, resulting in an eventual acquisition by McAfee, and initiated several thought leadership campaigns with media placements in CNN, NPR and hundreds of media outlets worldwide.As PR Director at leading antivirus provider Panda Security, her team successfully launched a leading edge artificial intelligence “zero-day attack” solution, resulting in multiple prestigious product awards and 84,000 media outlet placements, including PC World’s coveted “Best Buy” cover story, DowJones.com, Financial Times, CNN and others, reaching millions worldwide in less than one year.

about_text: Brenda Christensen is CEO of Stellar Public Relations, a world leader in public relations, investor relations, branding, funding and corporate guidance with direct attributable growth worth over millions of dollars. Ms. Christensen currently serves as an adviser on private boards in North America, and previously served as corporate officer for a publicly held technology company, across multiple continents.A leading corporate communications and public relations expert, board member and corporate officer of top global technology companies, Brenda has provided strategic corporate guidance and governance, as well as successfully created and managed global messaging campaigns for such prestigious companies as Tinder, Apple, McAfee, Panda Security, NEC, GM and others.In March 2020, she was named "Top 15 in Security PR" by noted author and cybersecurity thought leader, Richard Stiennon, voted “PR SourceCode Top 10 Tech Communicators” by 800 leading journalists and bloggers, as well as “Best PR in Tech” by Robert Scoble. In addition, she is listed as a top PR pro to follow on Twitter by Business2Community and HubSpot named her one of the “Most Influential on Facebook." Ms. Christensen was selected by The Economist for its prestigious cybersecurity simulation panel, including Richard A. Clarke, chief counter-terrorism advisor under George W. Bush for the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks (https://www.dailymotion.com/video/x6fblpu).As PR Director for Secure Computing, she orchestrated a successful post-acquisition restructuring of global public relations, resulting in an eventual acquisition by McAfee, and initiated several thought leadership campaigns with media placements in CNN, NPR and hundreds of media outlets worldwide.As PR Director at leading antivirus provider Panda Security, her team successfully launched a leading edge artificial intelligence “zero-day attack” solution, resulting in multiple prestigious product awards and 84,000 media outlet placements, including PC World’s coveted “Best Buy” cover story, DowJones.com, Financial Times, CNN and others, reaching millions worldwide in less than one year.

About: Dame Vivian Hunt is the Chief Innovation Officer at UnitedHealth Group. In this new role, she will work with their technology, growth and strategy teams to pursue new technologies, improve process design, interpret data, apply insights and improve the productivity of their systems.Before joining UnitedHealth Group, Dame Vivian served as a Senior Partner for McKinsey & Company, UK and Ireland, where she provided strategic advice to leading firms in the private, public and third sectors, with a particular focus on strategy, innovation and performance transformation. Dame Vivian also served as Managing Partner for the UK and Ireland for seven years from 2013-2020 and prior to that led the firm’s EMEA Life Sciences practice. Workplace: Best-Selling Author of "Inclusion on Purpose"
About: Roo-CHEEK-ah (phonetic like it's spelled. :) ) Black Lives Matter.Ruchika Tulshyan is the best-selling author of "Inclusion on Purpose: An Intersectional Approach to Creating a Culture of Belonging at Work,” published by MIT Press and available now. The book was called “transformative” by Dr. Brené Brown.Close to 150,000 learners have taken her first LinkedIn Learning course, “Moving DEI from Intention to Impact.”Ruchika is also the founder of Candour, a global inclusion strategy firm. She is a regular contributor to Harvard Business Review and the New York Times.Ruchika co-wrote a paradigm-shifting article, ‘Stop Telling Women They Have Imposter Syndrome’ for Harvard Business Review, with Jodi-Ann Burey. The article was named among 20 most impactful HBR articles of all time. Best of all, people all over the world have said it helped change their relationship with the concept of imposter syndrome!Ruchika is honored to be a LinkedIn Top Voice for Gender Equality in 2022. She was selected to Thinkers50 Radar 2019 and Hive Learning's Most Influential D&I leaders list for the past four years. In 2022, she received the Jeanette Williams Award from Seattle Women’s Commission for her work on advancing gender equality in the region.Ruchika is an active investor in various women-founded ventures, including Armoire, Graham & Walker VC and Backstage Capital. She has also been adjunct faculty in Communications at University of Washington and Seattle University. Ruchika previously wrote, “The Diversity Advantage: Fixing Gender Inequality in the Workplace.” A global citizen and Singaporean foodie, Ruchika has lived in five countries. She currently calls Seattle home.

Workplace: Founder and CEO, The Rural Beacon Initiative, LLC.
Location: Chapel Hill, North Carolina, United States
About: William J. Barber III grew up in eastern North Carolina, where, under the tutelage of his father, Bishop William J. Barber II and mother, Rebecca Barber, he developed at an early age a deep commitment to social justice and environmental stewardship. He now works as an environmental and climate justice scholar and advocate, with nearly a decade of social justice organizing experience and deep academic training in both the science and the law behind environmental and climate issues.William received his B.S. in Environmental Physics from North Carolina Central University and earned his juris doctorate from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill School of law, where he focused on environmental law and policy. He currently works as the Director of Climate and Environmental Justice at The Climate Reality Project, a non-profit based in Washington, D.C. whose mission is to catalyze a global solution to the climate crisis. He also serves as a member of the North Carolina Department of Environmental Quality Secretary's Environmental Justice and Equity Advisory Board, as well as co-chair for the North Carolina Poor People’s Campaign Ecological Devastation committee. William has several years of experience in grassroots and community organizing, working as a field secretary for the North Carolina NAACP for two years and serving as one of a three-member leadership team for Moral Freedom Summer, a long-term voter mobilization campaign spearheaded by the North Carolina NAACP.    He also worked and collaborated with his father and the Poor People's Campaign to cultivate a partnership with The Climate Reality Project focused on environmental justice. Most recently, he founded The Rural Beacon Initiative, LLC—a multi-member startup that provides consultation for groups looking to advance equity, climate justice, and environmental justice. Rural Beacon has evolved, exploring the role of green finance as a vehicle to address social disparities. He is interested in the renewable energy field and clean economy, specifically in initiatives that are being taken to promote opportunity for low-income communities and communities of color.He is also heavily interested in environmental policy, having completed work with several environmental advocacy groups, including the UNC Law Center for Climate, Energy, Environment, and Economics; Clean Water for North Carolina; Clean Energy Works, and the Coalition for Green Capital.

Introduction: Full Name: William J. Barber III | Workplace: Founder and CEO, The Rural Beacon Initiative, LLC. | Location: Chapel Hill, North Carolina, United States | Connections: 500+ | Photo: Yes
About: William J. Barber III grew up in eastern North Carolina, where, under the tutelage of his father, Bishop William J. Barber II and mother, Rebecca Barber, he developed at an early age a deep commitment to social justice and environmental stewardship. He now works as an environmental and climate justice scholar and advocate, with nearly a decade of social justice organizing experience and deep academic training in both the science and the law behind environmental and climate issues.William received his B.S. in Environmental Physics from North Carolina Central University and earned his juris doctorate from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill School of law, where he focused on environmental law and policy. He currently works as the Director of Climate and Environmental Justice at The Climate Reality Project, a non-profit based in Washington, D.C. whose mission is to catalyze a global solution to the climate crisis. He also serves as a member of the North Carolina Department of Environmental Quality Secretary's Environmental Justice and Equity Advisory Board, as well as co-chair for the North Carolina Poor People’s Campaign Ecological Devastation committee. William has several years of experience in grassroots and community organizing, working as a field secretary for the North Carolina NAACP for two years and serving as one of a three-member leadership team for Moral Freedom Summer, a long-term voter mobilization campaign spearheaded by the North Carolina NAACP. He also worked and collaborated with his father and the Poor People's Campaign to cultivate a partnership with The Climate Reality Project focused on environmental justice. Most recently, he founded The Rural Beacon Initiative, LLC—a multi-member startup that provides consultation for groups looking to advance equity, climate justice, and environmental justice. Rural Beacon has evolved, exploring the role of green finance as a vehicle to address social disparities. He is interested in the renewable energy field and clean economy, specifically in initiatives that are being taken to promote opportunity for low-income communities and communities of color.He is also heavily interested in environmental policy, having completed work with several environmental advocacy groups, including the UNC Law Center for Climate, Energy, Environment, and Economics; Clean Water for North Carolina; Clean Energy Works, and the Coalition for Green Capital.

About: Poornima is the author of 'Diversifying Diversity: Your guide to Being an Active Ally of Inclusion in the Workplace' and 'The Art of Active Allyship'. She is also the author of the HBR articles 'Do your global teams see DEI as an American issue?' and '7 ways to practice active allyship', and a TEDx speaker. Poornima is also the recipient of the Professional Women of Colour Denmark 2021 Impact award, and a finalist in the Trailblazer category of the 2022 Nordic Blaze Inclusion Awards.  Poornima has recently been recognised as one of the world's 30 most influential management thinkers by Thinkers50. She is currently writing her third book in this field, Leading through Bias. Poornima is Associate Professor at the Copenhagen Business School, and is a practioner-academic, effectively bringing together academic rigor with practical application. She draws on eighteen years of research and teaching experience and expertise in the field of talent management and DEI in Asia and Europe when engaging with companies and institutions in both the private and public sector. Poornima is also the founder of TalentED Consultancy to provide effective Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI) thought-leadership, workshops and consultancy services for organisations who are determined to nurture inclusive workplaces for their diverse talent. A passionate eductaor at heart, Poornima’s efforts in DEI focus on three main areas: (1) Expanding the dimensions of diversity we are inclusive to, with a focus on intersectionality, (2) Empowering individuals to be active allies of inclusion, and (3) Enabling inclusive leadership.Poornima delivers on her vision through keynotes, talks, workshops, books and articles, blog posts and podcasts.  In her keynotes, talks and workshops, Poornima leverages research, data, personal narratives, videos, as well as activities to create an engaging, psychologically safe and transformative experience. Poornima also condutcs DEI audits for organisations, working collaboratively with clients to develop their own unqiue DEI strategy and roadmap. Over the years, Poornima has worked with well-known organistaions across various industries and geographical contexts. These include Carlsberg, Novo Nordisk, Reckitt, KPMG, FedEx, deloitte, McCormick, Ørsted, L’Oreal, Amazon Web Services, Danske Bank, Medicines sans Frontiers (Doctors without Borders) amongst others.When Poornima isn’t engaging in DEI, she relishes spending time with her husband and two boys going for walks and hikes in nature, traveling, and cooking plant-based meals in the kitchen.

I am a frequent guest speaker on a variety of accounting topics for industry organizations and KPMG seminars. KPMG has invested in deep and broad services designed to solve complex business problems and I am passionate about connecting these solutions to the market and to delivering on KPMG’s commitment to high-quality service to our clients.I am actively involved in KPMG’s Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion priorities and work to unlock the power of all of our people. As a national leader in KPMG’s African Ancestry Business Resource Group I am invested in recruiting, mentoring, and developing professionals from underrepresented groups.I believe in supporting our communities and I am currently active with the Partnership for New York City as a 2022 David Rockefeller Fellow. This one-year program convenes private sector executives to learn about the city and state and build civic leadership skills. I also serve on the boards of the Greenwich Boys and Girls Club and New York Road Runners. I am an avid runner and in 2016, competed in the Abbott World Marathon Majors, which challenges runners to complete six of the largest and most renowned marathons in the world (Tokyo, Boston, London, Berlin, Chicago, and New York City) in a single calendar year. I was the 8th person in the world to complete the Majors. I was subsequently featured in a New York Times article, “When Gluttony Dons Racing Shoes,” written by Lindsay Crouse.

Today, the top 10 in-demand jobs weren’t jobs in 2004. And 6 years from now, students who graduate college today, may find the careers they are entering just might not exist. Career coaches, employment professionals, academia, government, and even faith-based institutions around the world need to understand this... and prepare people (and themselves) for this MAJOR SHIFT that is here to stay. about_text: Elizabeth (Lizz) Rene (she/her/hers) identifies as a Black woman who has dedicated her work full-time to dismantling oppressive systems and amplifying the stories of the Black community. She has worked for Google since April 2022. In her current role as an Equity Learning & Development (L&D) Program Manager, Lizz leads cross-functional working groups to center equity principles in L&D work and performance management systems. Prior to joining Google, Lizz served on the Equity Strategy and Programming Team for District of Columbia Public Schools (DCPS) providing strategic support and professional development around race, equity, diversity, and inclusion. She is a graduate of the University of Georgia, founding member of the Gathering Spot (Washington, DC), life-long member of Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Incorporated and a LUMA-certified Human Centered Design Practitioner.

About: Olesea Azevedo serves as Chief People Officer for AdventHealth, one of the largest faith-based health care systems in the United States. With over 80,000 team members in 50 hospitals and 73 medical facilities across nine states, AdventHealth provides communities with a whole-person care experience. Since joining AdventHealth in 2016, Azevedo has built and championed the People and Culture team through integrating a shared services model. Azevedo is a founding member and co-sponsor of AdventHealth’s Leadership Institute, which is responsible for advancing internal leadership development. Azevedo, in partnership with the CEO, also established DEI councils in every market to advocate organizational diversity and inclusion. Through innovative design and amplifying team member’s voice, Azevedo has led the organization’s bold Team Member Promise aspiration, working to develop a unique team member experience and a culture of personal and professional well-being. Azevedo is actively involved with various boards and organizations, including AdventHealth University, Waterman Hospital, and Hearts in Unison. Azevedo has been recognized by multiple organizations, including Top 100 HR Professionals from OnCon Conference (2022), Talent Acquisition Team of the Year (2021), and Elite Talent Acquisition Organization from Lean Human Capital (2020).

Introduction: Full Name: Olesea Azevedo | Workplace: Chief People Officer at AdventHealth | Location: Altamonte Springs, Florida, United States | Connections: 500+ | Photo: Yes
About: Olesea Azevedo serves as Chief People Officer for AdventHealth, one of the largest faith-based health care systems in the United States. With over 80,000 team members in 50 hospitals and 73 medical facilities across nine states, AdventHealth provides communities with a whole-person care experience. Since joining AdventHealth in 2016, Azevedo has built and championed the People and Culture team through integrating a shared services model. Azevedo is a founding member and co-sponsor of AdventHealth’s Leadership Institute, which is responsible for advancing internal leadership development. Azevedo, in partnership with the CEO, also established DEI councils in every market to advocate organizational diversity and inclusion. Through innovative design and amplifying team member’s voice, Azevedo has led the organization’s bold Team Member Promise aspiration, working to develop a unique team member experience and a culture of personal and professional well-being. Azevedo is actively involved with various boards and organizations, including AdventHealth University, Waterman Hospital, and Hearts in Unison. Azevedo has been recognized by multiple organizations, including Top 100 HR Professionals from OnCon Conference (2022), Talent Acquisition Team of the Year (2021), and Elite Talent Acquisition Organization from Lean Human Capital (2020).

Introduction: Full Name: Oliver Queen, Jr. | Workplace: Independent Consultant (Acquisition, Program Management, Procurement, Supply Chain and Logistics, Knowledge Management) | Location: Washington, District of Columbia, United States | Connections: 500+ | Photo: Yes
About: Senior Acquisition Consultant, former Director of Supply Chain and Logistics, and Military Veteran currently holding an active security clearance offering over 29 years of experience in Supply Chain and Logistics Management, Program Management, Government and Commercial Acquisition and Contracting, Executive Leadership, and Business Operations expertise in both the government and private sectors. Managed risk along multiple lines and provided managerial review and approval oversight of all mission-critical requirements totaling over $1.7 Billion dollars directly to the Head of Contracting Authority and Secretary of the Navy. Also, developed investment evaluation architecture to compete a $7M Business IT Support Services contract critical to MSC Worldwide Operations and a $37 Million Dollar Financial Services Re-compete in support of the Department of the Interior, Office of the Secretary. Provided timely recommendations and innovative acquisition solutions to negotiate multiple simplified acquisitions totaling $2.5M+. Executed several service contract actions totaling over $110M and demonstrated exceptional skills in drafting business clearances in support of challenging negotiations by critically analyzing and identifying errors in the profit percentages; resulted in a 32 % savings to the government. Attended Leadership of the 21st Century: Chaos, Conflict, and Courage” seminar at the John F Kennedy School of Government at Harvard University; currently working as a Senior Acquisition Consultant in Washington DC. Possess a comprehensive background in talent management and coaching, research and data analytics, organizational analysis, team integration, leadership development, strategy development/process mapping, operational budget management, leadership and executive training development and delivery, and personnel management derived from the United States Navy.

Introduction: Full Name: Andrea Pipitone Beirne | Workplace: Partner at KPMG US | Location: Greater Chicago Area | Connections: 500+ | Photo: Yes
About: Andrea is the national lead partner for the Lender Due Diligence group at KPMG. Andrea has 27 years of professional service experience, including five years of auditing of SEC registered companies. The Lender Due Diligence group specialized in financial due diligence performed in conjunction leveraged financing. The group has substantial experience with global manufacturing, retail and distribution companies. Andrea is a Certified Public Accountant and Certified Insolvency and Restructuring Advisor, as well as a member of the AICPA, Illinois CPA Society, CIRA and Education board member for the Commercial Finance Association.Specialties: Andrea’s financial due diligence experience includes analyzing and modeling structured finance transactions, evaluating asset-based and cash-flow debt structures, and assisting acquirers in financial, cost saving and synergy analysis. Andrea has diverse experience in manufacturing, distribution, chemicals, agriculture and retail segments.In addition, Andrea has five years of experience providing financial statement audit services to publicly traded companies while at Arthur Andersen.

Publications: Publication: 0: 0: Title: A Manganese-Doped Barium Carbonate Cathode for Alkaline Batteries | 0: Journal: Journal of The Electrochemical Society · Mar 27, 2014 | 0: Description: MnO2-Zn alkaline batteries are one of the most common modern forms of primary battery, due to their relatively high energy density and low cost per kilowatt-hour. Additionally, unlike many other types of primary battery, alkaline cells can theoretically be recharged. Their low cost per kilowatt-hour makes them potentially ideal for applications such as sustainable energy storage or peak demand shaving. However, a phase transformation that occurs in MnO2 after reduction by more than one electron converts it into the electrochemically inactive Mn3O4 phase. This limits the total depth of discharge of the cell signiﬁcantly. We report the synthesis of a novel electrode material, manganese-doped witherite, for rechargeable alkaline batteries produced by a simple hydrothermal process. The material has been studied via X-ray diffraction and electroanalytical techniques. We show that unaltered witherite has poor electrochemical properties, and that this new material has high capacity and rate capability, even under deep discharge conditions, superior to conventional manganese dioxide. | Publication: 1: 1: Title: Real-time materials evolution visualized within intact cycling alkaline batteries | 1: Journal: Journal of Materials Chemistry A · Jan 1, 2014 | 1: Description: The scientific community has focused on the problem of inexpensive, safe, and sustainable large-scale electrical energy storage, which is needed for a number of emerging societal reasons such as stabilizing intermittent renewables-based generation like solar and wind power. The materials used for large-scale storage will need to be low cost, earth-abundant, and safe at the desired scale. The Zn–MnO2 “alkaline” battery chemistry is associated with one-time use, despite being rechargeable. This is due to material irreversibilities that can be triggered in either the anode or cathode. However, as Zn and MnO2 have high energy density and low cost, they are economically attractive even at limited depth of discharge. As received, a standard bobbin-type alkaline cell costs roughly $20 per kW h. The U.S. Department of Energy ARPA-E $100 per kW h cost target for grid storage is thus close to the cost of alkaline consumer primary cells if re-engineered and/or cycled at 5–20% nominal capacity. Herein we use a deeply-penetrating in situ technique to observe ZnO precipitation near the separator in an alkaline cell anode cycled at 5% DOD, which is consistent with cell failures observed at high cycle life. Alkaline cells designed to avoid such causes of cell failure could serve as a low-cost baseload for large-scale storage. | Publication: 2: 2: Title: An In Situ Synchrotron Study of Zinc Anode Planarization by a Bismuth Additive | 2: Journal: Journal of the Electrochemical Society · Dec 21, 2013 | 2: Description: Cyclic voltammetry of zinc plated from flowing alkaline zincate electrolyte with a bismuth additive showed a marked mass transport effect during metal layer deplating. This bismuth was added as Bi2O3 and had a saturated concentration of 26 ppm bismuth. Using a small, transparent window flow cell the mechanism was studied in situ using synchrotron X-rays. X-ray microdiffraction revealed that the metal-electrolyte interface was bismuth rich, and bismuth behaved in a manner similar to a surfactant. Transmission X-ray microscopy revealed that in the presence of bismuth additive, 5 μm raised features on the metal layer were preferentially dissolved during deplating. However, macro-morphology experiments demonstrated that at 26 ppm a detrimental bismuth buildup occurred over many cycles. By reducing additive concentration to 3 ppm a metal layer was planarized compared to a no-additive control, while avoiding the bismuth buildup. These findings suggested that 3 ppm bismuth could be used to planarize zinc metal layers such as those in flow-assisted zinc batteries. However, concentration will need to be well-controlled.

intro_text: Full Name: Kelvin Vi Luan Tran | Workplace: Chief Financial Officer at TD | Location: Canada | Connections: 500+ | Photo: No
about_text: I joined TD over 20 years ago and have developed my career holding progressively senior roles. Currently, I serve as TD's Chief Financial Officer and I'm a member of the Bank's Senior Executive Team. As CFO, I oversee TD's Finance, Investor Relations, Enterprise Strategy and Global tax functions, as well as the Chief Accountant's Department. My team is focused on the Bank's financial standing and performance, ensuring financial reporting accuracy, regulatory compliance and the integrity of our processes and practices to ensure we deliver for customers, colleagues and shareholders. Previously I served as TD's Head of Enterprise Finance, Chief Financial Officer for TD Bank, America’s Most Convenient Bank®, Chief Auditor for TD, CFO of TD Securities and SVP of Treasury and Balance Sheet Management.Both inside the Bank and within the community, I'm an active supporter of diversity and inclusion. I was proud to serve as the founding President of Ascend Canada, a not-for-profit organization focused on developing pan-Asian leaders. At TD, I have Chaired both the TD Visible Minority Committee as well as the Diversity Leadership Council of the Office of the CFO within the TD community.Previously, I was a member of the Board of Directors of Diabetes Canada and past Chair of their Audit Committee. I was also a community member of the Finance and Audit Committee for the Markham Stouffville Hospital and previously served as Treasurer and Chair of the Finance, Pension and Audit Committee for the Board of Regents of Victoria University, in the University of Toronto.If you're interested in learning more about opportunities at TD, please visit our career site: jobs.td.com.

about_text: As a member of KPMG’s global life sciences leadership team, I build approaches, tools, and solutions that drive value for pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and medical technology businesses. My commitment to client service in Healthcare has earned my inclusion in Consulting Magazine’s list of “Top 25 Consultants” in the country. With 25+ years of experience employing innovative solutions, I lead teams that help life science companies succeed in our new reality of continual disruption. I guide strategies to transform global operating models, launch new products, manage risks, handle mergers and acquisitions, and implement and leverage innovative technologies, data sciences and automation across the Life Science value chain. I am proud to serve on the Advisory Board of the Healthcare Businesswomen’s Association, the steering committee of the NJ Women’s Network to Network organization and as a member of the KPMG Network of Women. I am proud to have been named one of the "Best 50 Women in Business in New Jersey", and as a "Healthcare Businesswomen's Association Rising Star".

About: I am an authentic and relatable inclusion, diversity and equity focused consultant. Through training, coaching, and speaking, I help organizations, diversity and inclusion leaders and high achievers appropriately disrupt the status quo to invite the innovation, momentum and the diversity of thought necessary to achieve their inclusion goals.A people passionate, idea-generating, strategist, I develop inclusive leaders and cultivate diverse and equitable cultures for Fortune 500 Organizations with as much as $50B in sales and small 5-person organizations. Through the application of new and existing knowledge, and my knack for creating vulnerable spaces, I bring safety, authenticity and honesty to difficult topics. Together we will shift narratives, broaden perspectives and bring about mindset-shifts on subjects such as:Diversity & InclusionUnconscious BiasIntersectionalityLearning & DevelopmentLeadership BehaviorsTeam BuildingMentoring Resources & ProgrammingOnboarding Customized Training Delivery Talent Management Program & Project Management Strategic PlanningChange ManagementAs a servant leader on non-profit boards including Brown Girls Do Ballet, a former Proud Walmart Associate, and the founder of a diversity and inclusion-focused HR consulting firm, Cabral Co, I am able to combine big strategic thinking, creative, cost-saving approaches and nimble start-up energy to tailoring solutions for an organization's unique needs. I partner with corporate entities, non-profits, and educational institutions to incite inclusive behavior changes that create a sense of belonging for everyone.Let's connect!

About: Quinetta Roberson, Ph.D. is the John A. Hannah Distinguished Professor of Management and Psychology, prior to which she was on the faculty at Villanova University and Cornell University. She has been a visiting scholar at universities on six continents and has more than 20 years of global experience in teaching courses, facilitating workshops, and advising organizations on leadership, talent management and diversity. Dr. Roberson has published over 40 scholarly journal articles and book chapters, and edited a Handbook of Diversity in the Workplace (2013). Her research and consulting work focus on developing organizational capability and enhancing effectiveness through the strategic management of people, particularly diverse work teams, and is informed by her background in finance, having worked as a financial analyst and small business development consultant prior to obtaining her doctorate.  She earned her Ph.D. in Organizational Behavior from the University of Maryland, and holds undergraduate and graduate degrees in Finance.

Workplace: Fortune 500 Director | Former Global Chief DEI Officer, Coca-Cola | Inspiring Speaker | ESG Advisor | Driving Strategic Communications | Amplifying Diverse Voices
About: Lori George Billingsley is the former Global Chief Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI) Officer for The Coca-Cola Company (TCCC).  In that role, she led the company’s DEI Center of Excellence, all directed to enable a more engaged global workforce, mirror the markets served, and support a more inclusive culture to best position the employees of the company to drive growth.  She was with the company for 20 years, having spent most of them in a variety of roles with increasing responsibility within Public Affairs and Communications. Lori has over 30 years of public affairs, issues communications, community and stakeholder relations, social impact and diversity, equity and inclusion experience in developing and implementing breakthrough strategic initiatives that meet organizational goals, target audience needs and produce results. Prior to joining Coca-Cola, she led her own public relations consultancy, LG Communications; was a vice president at Porter/Novelli, a leading public relations firm where she co-founded their Multicultural Communications and Alliance Building practices. She currently serves on the Board of Directors of Pioneer Natural Resources (NYSE: PXD), Shake Shack (NYSE: SHAK), NAACP Foundation and Arete Executive Women of Influence. She is a member of the National Association of Corporate Director’s Center for Inclusive Governance Advisory Council, Howard University’s School of Communications Board of Visitors, Executive Leadership Council, OnBoard, International Women’s Forum and IWIN Advisory Board Committee.Former boards served on include Boards of the Congressional Black Caucus Foundation, Inc. (Chair), Women’s Business Enterprise National Council, United Way of Greater Atlanta, Atlanta Mission, Leadership Atlanta, ColorComm and The Coca-Cola Foundation. She also served on the World Economic Forum’s (WEF) Partnering for Racial Justice in Business Advisory Council, WEF’s Community of Chief Diversity & Inclusion Officers, The Conference Board DEI Innovators Council and as Co-Chair of American University’s Inaugural Women’s Network and Co-Chair of the TCCC’s Political Action Committee.She received her Bachelor of Arts in public relations at Howard University and her Master of Arts in public communications at American University. about_text: Lori George Billingsley is the former Global Chief Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI) Officer for The Coca-Cola Company (TCCC). In that role, she led the company’s DEI Center of Excellence, all directed to enable a more engaged global workforce, mirror the markets served, and support a more inclusive culture to best position the employees of the company to drive growth. She was with the company for 20 years, having spent most of them in a variety of roles with increasing responsibility within Public Affairs and Communications. Lori has over 30 years of public affairs, issues communications, community and stakeholder relations, social impact and diversity, equity and inclusion experience in developing and implementing breakthrough strategic initiatives that meet organizational goals, target audience needs and produce results. Prior to joining Coca-Cola, she led her own public relations consultancy, LG Communications; was a vice president at Porter/Novelli, a leading public relations firm where she co-founded their Multicultural Communications and Alliance Building practices. She currently serves on the Board of Directors of Pioneer Natural Resources (NYSE: PXD), Shake Shack (NYSE: SHAK), NAACP Foundation and Arete Executive Women of Influence. She is a member of the National Association of Corporate Director’s Center for Inclusive Governance Advisory Council, Howard University’s School of Communications Board of Visitors, Executive Leadership Council, OnBoard, International Women’s Forum and IWIN Advisory Board Committee.Former boards served on include Boards of the Congressional Black Caucus Foundation, Inc. (Chair), Women’s Business Enterprise National Council, United Way of Greater Atlanta, Atlanta Mission, Leadership Atlanta, ColorComm and The Coca-Cola Foundation. She also served on the World Economic Forum’s (WEF) Partnering for Racial Justice in Business Advisory Council, WEF’s Community of Chief Diversity & Inclusion Officers, The Conference Board DEI Innovators Council and as Co-Chair of American University’s Inaugural Women’s Network and Co-Chair of the TCCC’s Political Action Committee.She received her Bachelor of Arts in public relations at Howard University and her Master of Arts in public communications at American University. In 2019, she completed a 13-month Executive Leadership Experience Program at Harvard Business School; and in 2021, she completed Stanford University Graduate School of Business Directors’ Consortium. Lori is an ordained minister and mentor and loves to travel and spend time on the beach.

About: Lisa W. Wardell is former executive chairman of Adtalem Global Education’s board of directors.Adtalem Global Education Inc. (NYSE: ATGE) is a leading workforce solutions provider and the parent organization of American University of the Caribbean School of Medicine, ACAMS, Chamberlain University, Ross University School of Medicine, Ross University School of Veterinary Medicine and Walden University.Wardell was appointed executive chairman of the board in 2021. In her role as executive chairman, Wardell leads the board of directors and helps guide the company’s mission and strategy, as well as continues to represent the company and interact with key stakeholders to help advance Adtalem’s mission. Wardell has been part of Adtalem’s board since 2008, most recently serving as chairman of the board since 2019.In addition to her role on Adtalem’s board, Wardell served as president and CEO of Adtalem from 2016 to 2021. During her tenure as CEO, Wardell oversaw the strategic repositioning of Adtalem’s portfolio, successfully acquiring and integrating companies in Adtalem’s financial services vertical, and leading turnarounds and divestitures of Adtalem’s non-core assets. Through her commitment to high performance and positive social impact, Lisa’s leadership has resulted in superior outcomes for Adtalem’s students, significant value creation for shareholders and positioned the company for long-term growth.Prior to joining Adtalem, Wardell was executive vice president and chief operating officer for The RLJ Companies. As COO, Wardell was responsible for managing The RLJ Companies portfolio, including strategic partnerships, mergers and acquisitions, business strategy, operations and finance. Prior to joining The RLJ Companies, Wardell was a principal at Katalyst Venture Partners, a private equity firm that invested in start-up technology companies, and a senior consultant for Accenture.Wardell serves on the boards of American Express (NYSE: AXP), GIII Apparel  Group (NYSE: GIII); and Adtalem Global Education (NYSE: ATGE. She serves as a board member for Chamberlain University and Walden University.  Wardell is a member of The Business Council, a vice chair of the Kennedy Center Corporate Fund, and is a member of the board of the Economic Club of Chicago, the Executive Leadership Council, CEO Action for Diversity and Inclusion and the Fortune CEO Initiative. Additionally, Wardell has been featured on CNBC as well as in The Wall Street Journal, Washington Post, Business Insider, Black Enterprise, Cheddar and other publications.

She brings global perspective and extraordinary cross-cultural understanding to how we see, think about, struggle with and ultimately forge relationships with change. April also harnesses her very personal experiences with flux, including the death of both of her parents in a car accident when she was 20. Her mission is to connect people, ideas and resources in ways that say "wow, that's what the world needs" and "wow, we'd never seen it that way" -- and then to see differently and make it happen.

About: I, Monica Poulard Hawkins is Founder, CEO and Connector of Professional Pipeline Development Group (PPDG), a boutique management consulting firm that houses world-class thought leaders, strategists, and business executives in serving its client base of Fortune & Global 1000 Corporations, Heads of State, and Non-Profits.  We work to help them reimagine their organizations for the future ad build capacity for impact in new ways.It has been an honor to gain a reputation through servant leadership and drive purposeful growth. My sweet spot is in disruptive intersections of discovery, bumping up against tradition to actually support leaders in "doing" what they say they want and need through people who may be stuck, resistant, hesitant, comfortable or just plain don't want to.  It is the willing "hidden figures" that bring vision to life. I am known for telling the hard truths, and taking on the hard stuff.  In doing so,  together we change the world for the better.  The world needs authentic leaders who are purpose-driven and willing to coach teams through. I am the daughter and niece of leaders who served with  Rev. Dr. Martin Luther King, interned with Rev Gardner C. Taylor, and sat on Congressional and Senatorial Committees advocating for equality and justice in multiple sectors.   Growing up and through the strength and emotional trauma of my family gave me skills, tools, perspective, and a voice which makes me willing and able to support global leaders bridge and translate their truths with and amongst each other.  This manifested early in my career as I was assigned to lead a body of work while working at the U.S. Department of State commencing with Nelson Mandela’s release from prison, to his election as President through his first U.S. Head of State visit.   It continued while managing the communications between two CEOs during a Corporate Merger in the Telecom Industry. Today, I am invited into the metaverse,  I love living in our Moonshot Lab- (X-In Black). Most of all, I feel in this season, emerging scholars and early career leaders desire to live and work on purpose. about_text: I, Monica Poulard Hawkins is Founder, CEO and Connector of Professional Pipeline Development Group (PPDG), a boutique management consulting firm that houses world-class thought leaders, strategists, and business executives in serving its client base of Fortune & Global 1000 Corporations, Heads of State, and Non-Profits. We work to help them reimagine their organizations for the future ad build capacity for impact in new ways.It has been an honor to gain a reputation through servant leadership and drive purposeful growth. My sweet spot is in disruptive intersections of discovery, bumping up against tradition to actually support leaders in "doing" what they say they want and need through people who may be stuck, resistant, hesitant, comfortable or just plain don't want to. It is the willing "hidden figures" that bring vision to life. I am known for telling the hard truths, and taking on the hard stuff. In doing so, together we change the world for the better. The world needs authentic leaders who are purpose-driven and willing to coach teams through. I am the daughter and niece of leaders who served with Rev. Dr. Martin Luther King, interned with Rev Gardner C. Taylor, and sat on Congressional and Senatorial Committees advocating for equality and justice in multiple sectors. Growing up and through the strength and emotional trauma of my family gave me skills, tools, perspective, and a voice which makes me willing and able to support global leaders bridge and translate their truths with and amongst each other. This manifested early in my career as I was assigned to lead a body of work while working at the U.S. Department of State commencing with Nelson Mandela’s release from prison, to his election as President through his first U.S. Head of State visit. It continued while managing the communications between two CEOs during a Corporate Merger in the Telecom Industry. Today, I am invited into the metaverse, I love living in our Moonshot Lab- (X-In Black). Most of all, I feel in this season, emerging scholars and early career leaders desire to live and work on purpose. Supporting them in their journey to greatness as they navigate the future of work is what I am here for it. All day, every day.We have work to do leaders. And any creativity you had is interrupted. Your people want to see how your leaders can navigate through this season and value them as much as you value profit, on purpose.

I graduated from the Wharton School at the University of Pennsylvania, and I am a board member of the Advisory Board for the Life Sciences & Management Program at my alma mater.

Apart from my duties at AbbVie, I serve on the board of Aptinyx, where I am a member of the audit and compensation committees. I graduated from the Wharton School at the University of Pennsylvania, and I am a board member of the Advisory Board for the Life Sciences & Management Program at my alma mater.

About: For me, everyday starts at zero. By the end of the day I need to learn something new, assist a teammate, solve a problem, or find a strategic path forward to feel satisfied. about_text: Through his two decades of leadership at employers like EY, Deloitte, Costco Wholesale, GM Financial, and PRIDE Industries, Mr. Hediger is a well-rounded and trusted manager in IT security, privacy, cloud security, and GRC strategy (including: FEDRAMP, AICPA SOC II reporting, ISO 18000/27000/31000 series, DISA, FIPS 140-2 (encryption), COVID/CARES Act, PCI, HIPAA, GDPR, CoBIT, NIST, and CA Senate Bill 1386). In addition to being a well-regarded speaker, he has implemented and led teams for:. Three ERP implementations (one SAP, one Oracle, and one INFOR). Three ePrivacy implementations covering the GDPR via BigID and OneTrust. Three SIEM implementations (one Splunk, one LogRhythm, and one Rapid7). Three cloud integrations (focused on AWS EC2 and Lambda, MS Azure SQL, Azure Active Directory (AD), and data classification for GDPR). Two Identity and Access Management (IAM) implementations (both SailPoint Identity IQ single tenant on-premise and cloud). Two ServiceNow CMDB implementations. 30 GRC system implementations, including: 19 via RSA Archer , five via ACL, two via SAP GRC, one via MetricStream, one via Lockpath, one via ServiceNow GRC, and one via PolicyIQTim has significant experience working with offshore (India and the Philippines) and remote onshore (US) resources - along with client onsite resources. Mr. Hediger is a: * Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP);* Certified Information Systems Auditor (CISA);* Certified Internal Auditor (CIA);* Certified Fraud Examiner (CFE);* Certified in Control Self-Assessment (CCSA);* RSA Archer Certified Administrator (Version 5.x and 6.x);* ACL Certified Data Analyst (ACDA);* Certified in Risk Management Assurance (CRMA);* US Department of Defense Information Assurance Security Officer (DoD IASO);* ITIL Foundation Certified**Links and comments by Mr. Hediger do not necessarily reflect the views of his employers or any other affiliate**

About: Through his two decades of leadership at employers like EY, Deloitte, Costco Wholesale, GM Financial, and PRIDE Industries, Mr. Hediger is a well-rounded and trusted manager in IT security, privacy, cloud security, and GRC strategy (including: FEDRAMP, AICPA SOC II reporting, ISO 18000/27000/31000 series, DISA, FIPS 140-2 (encryption), COVID/CARES Act, PCI, HIPAA, GDPR, CoBIT, NIST, and CA Senate Bill 1386). In addition to being a well-regarded speaker, he has implemented and led teams for:. Three ERP implementations (one SAP, one Oracle, and one INFOR). Three ePrivacy implementations covering the GDPR via BigID and OneTrust. Three SIEM implementations (one Splunk, one LogRhythm, and one Rapid7). Three cloud integrations (focused on AWS EC2 and Lambda, MS Azure SQL, Azure Active Directory (AD), and data classification for GDPR). Two Identity and Access Management (IAM) implementations (both SailPoint Identity IQ single tenant on-premise and cloud). Two ServiceNow CMDB implementations. 30 GRC system implementations, including: 19 via RSA Archer , five via ACL, two via SAP GRC, one via MetricStream, one via Lockpath, one via ServiceNow GRC, and one via PolicyIQTim has significant experience working with offshore (India and the Philippines) and remote onshore (US) resources - along with client onsite resources. Mr. Hediger is a: * Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP);* Certified Information Systems Auditor (CISA);* Certified Internal Auditor (CIA);* Certified Fraud Examiner (CFE);* Certified in Control Self-Assessment (CCSA);* RSA Archer Certified Administrator (Version 5.x and 6.x);* ACL Certified Data Analyst (ACDA);* Certified in Risk Management Assurance (CRMA);* US Department of Defense Information Assurance Security Officer (DoD IASO);* ITIL Foundation Certified**Links and comments by Mr. Hediger do not necessarily reflect the views of his employers or any other affiliate**

About: As a first-generation college student, I learned to navigate the terrain of higher education. My ability to keep calm, assess situations, build a network, and gather the information I needed, allowed me to succeed in school. It also informs the work I do every day. I’ve made a career out of creating structure in ambiguous environments, designing operational roadmaps and setting the strategy for projects that allow companies to save money, improve productivity, and grow revenue. I not only have the technical depth to be able to understand and analyze the multiple moving parts of financial organizations, but also have the EQ and communication skills needed to craft a cohesive story with the data, negotiate partnerships, unite resources, and influence both stakeholders and decision makers on large, global initiatives. As a manager, I lead by lifting others up. I know that I’ve gotten to where I am with the support of family members, mentors and internal sponsors who have cheered me on, advised me and opened doors. I give back by helping others to navigate through gray areas by serving as a mentor, and by being involved in ISFFA (International Society of Filipinos in Finance and Accounting), where I founded the New York chapter and previously served as chapter President.

about_text: Chris Clements is a Fellow of the Institute of Chartered Accountants in England and Wales and partner at Deloitte. He has specialised as a Forensic Accountant since 1996 and has a breadth of experience in international arbitration, disputes, investigation, expert witness, ADR and advisory work. He also leads Deloitte's International Arbitration practice in the UK.He is an experienced Forensic Accountant expert witness has working knowledge of the legal process in International Arbitration matters (IBA, ICC, LCIA), Civil Disputes (CPR), Divorce disputes (FPR) and Criminal cases (CrPR). He is an individual member of the Expert Witness Institute, the Academy of Experts and the Chartered Institute of Arbitrators. He is also a qualified mediator. As a Forensic Accountant Chris is experienced in advisory, claimant, defence, disputes, international arbitration and investigation work involving claims of over STG£3bn. He has given evidence over 25 times in the UK and overseas in Courts (including High, Criminal, TCC, Family), Arbitrations (including ad hoc and International Arbitrations) and Tribunals. He has worked as a Forensic Accountant on assignments across the globe including in Canada, Cayman Islands, Egypt, Germany, India, Israel, Italy, Japan, Peru, Rumania, Saudi Arabia, Spain, Sweden, Thailand, UAE, and the USA.He has worked as a forensic accountant on litigation dispute and International Arbitration cases as single joint forensic accountancy dispute expert, as an dispute expert forensic accountant appointed by a single party; as an advisor/consulting expert forensic accountant, mediator and as expert determiner and arbitrator (including expert forensic accountant appointments by the president of the ICAEW). He can be contacted on chrisclements at deloitte.com or mobile +971 554832371 on WhatsApp +44 (0) 7968 33 88 95
