About: Dr. Tarika Barrett is the CEO of Girls Who Code, an international non-profit organization working to close the gender gap in technology by inspiring, educating and equipping young women with the computing skills to pursue 21st century opportunities. Prior to becoming CEO, Tarika served as Chief Operating Officer of the organization. She led the organization's free Summer Immersion Program and after-school Clubs Program, which has reached 500,000 girls around the world to date. Additionally, she managed the launch of international Programming, Alumni Programming, and managed the People & Culture team. Tarika has served on the boards of CSforALL, Eskolta, AT&T’s Accelerator Advisory Board, and McGraw Hill. Currently, she serves as a member of the Homeland Security Advisory Council (HSAC), as chair of the New York University Steinhardt Dean's Alumni Advisory Board, the New Visions for Public Schools Board of Directors, and as a member of the Eniac Ventures network. Tarika is the recipient of the New York University Steinhardt School Dorothy Height Distinguished Alumni Achievement Award and the New York City Bar Association Huntington Bank’s Her Hero Lifetime Achievement Award. She was named one of Crain’s 50 Most Powerful Women in New York in 2021, to the PoliticsNY and amNewYork 2022 Power Women list, and to City and State New York’s “Power of Diversity: Women 100 List.”Previously, Tarika worked as the Chief Program Officer at iMentor, leading the organization’s programmatic efforts to build mentoring relationships that support students from low-income communities in graduating high school and succeeding in college. Prior to iMentor, she worked in the Office of Postsecondary Readiness at the New York City Department of Education overseeing options for students significantly off-track academically, as well as developing new school models including the Academy for Software Engineering. Tarika’s previous experience includes serving as Deputy Network Leader of the Brooklyn-Staten Island Network of New Visions for Public Schools, designing and implementing research and program evaluations for New York University’s Center for Research on Teaching and Learning, teaching high school students, and working as a political organizer. A graduate of Brooklyn College, Tarika has an M.A. in Deaf Education from Columbia Teachers College and a Ph.D. in Teaching and Learning from New York University. Tarika lives in Brooklyn with her husband and two children.

Introduction: Full Name: Victoria Konkiel | Workplace: Software Engineer | Location: Minneapolis, Minnesota, United States | Connections: 355 | Photo: Yes
About: At heart, I love math and science. They were always my two favorite subjects to learn, and I still enjoy learning anything math and science related. I believe it is for this reason that I love being a software engineer! I feel very fortunate that I am able to incorporate skills from my previous careers like data analysis, logistics management, and design to help me thrive in my new career.I would have to say my love for computers came when I was in middle school and had the opportunity to major in communication arts. From building my first web page with GeoCities, being able to create something from (essentially) nothing has always been super rewarding and satisfying for me. While I lost my way as far as careers throughout my earlier life, I was ecstatic when I had the opportunity to join a coding boot camp when the pandemic was in its early stages. From that boot camp, I haven't looked back! I know being a software engineer is what I enjoy and want to do, so I look forward to learning as much as I can and using my knowledge and skillset to excel in this career path.

About: Dr. Saundra Wall Williams is an accomplished senior executive in higher education with over 25 years of extensive experience, achievements and demonstrated results as a leader, faculty member, mentor, coach, consultant, speaker and practitioner in higher education and technology. From 2001 until 2016, she was the Senior Vice President and Chief of Information Technology, Data, Business Intelligence, Library Systems, Distance Learning and Workforce Development for the North Carolina Community College System. She led the implementation of the largest computer information system in higher education, in addition to training and development, instructional technology, information technology systems implementation, information technology security, technology infrastructure, software design, digital transformation, distance learning, and data systems. While serving in numerous leadership roles, Dr. Saundra remained an active consulting partner focusing on leadership coaching.  She is currently the CEO and Founding Partner of WMS Consulting and Training, a professional development, consulting and training company that supports emerging and established women leaders to increase their influence, impact and income. She is a member of the Board of Trustees at Wake Technical Community College, Board of Directors for the Ultimate Medical Academy, NC State University College of Sciences Foundation Board, Public School Forum, and Girl Scouts – Coastal Pines. She is a member of the Steering Committee for Wake Invests in Women.Dr. Saundra is a Kellogg Foundation Houle Scholar in Adult Education, Azusa Scholar in Divinity, NC State University College of Sciences Alumni of the Year, North Carolina Chief Information Officer of the Year, North Carolina’s Technology Woman of the Year, North Carolina ACHI Magazine 2018 Woman of Achievement and 2019 NC State University Outstanding Black Alumni.A published researcher and author in her professional field of technology and adult education, she has written 3 books, co-authored 6 books and numerous articles and book chapters.Dr. Saundra is a graduate of NC State University with a BS in Mathematics, MS in Applied Mathematics and Statistics, and Doctor of Education in Adult and Community College Education. She holds a Master of Divinity from Regent University and was awarded the Honorary Associate of Science degree from Richmond Community College. She is a certified CIO with the State of NC through the University of NC at Chapel Hill, a certified Strengths Champion Certified Coach® and a certified Transformation Coach.

About: Dr. Saundra Wall Williams is an accomplished senior executive in higher education with over 25 years of extensive experience, achievements and demonstrated results as a leader, faculty member, mentor, coach, consultant, speaker and practitioner in higher education and technology. From 2001 until 2016, she was the Senior Vice President and Chief of Information Technology, Data, Business Intelligence, Library Systems, Distance Learning and Workforce Development for the North Carolina Community College System. She led the implementation of the largest computer information system in higher education, in addition to training and development, instructional technology, information technology systems implementation, information technology security, technology infrastructure, software design, digital transformation, distance learning, and data systems. While serving in numerous leadership roles, Dr. Saundra remained an active consulting partner focusing on leadership coaching. She is currently the CEO and Founding Partner of WMS Consulting and Training, a professional development, consulting and training company that supports emerging and established women leaders to increase their influence, impact and income. She is a member of the Board of Trustees at Wake Technical Community College, Board of Directors for the Ultimate Medical Academy, NC State University College of Sciences Foundation Board, Public School Forum, and Girl Scouts – Coastal Pines. She is a member of the Steering Committee for Wake Invests in Women.Dr. Saundra is a Kellogg Foundation Houle Scholar in Adult Education, Azusa Scholar in Divinity, NC State University College of Sciences Alumni of the Year, North Carolina Chief Information Officer of the Year, North Carolina’s Technology Woman of the Year, North Carolina ACHI Magazine 2018 Woman of Achievement and 2019 NC State University Outstanding Black Alumni.A published researcher and author in her professional field of technology and adult education, she has written 3 books, co-authored 6 books and numerous articles and book chapters.Dr. Saundra is a graduate of NC State University with a BS in Mathematics, MS in Applied Mathematics and Statistics, and Doctor of Education in Adult and Community College Education. She holds a Master of Divinity from Regent University and was awarded the Honorary Associate of Science degree from Richmond Community College. She is a certified CIO with the State of NC through the University of NC at Chapel Hill, a certified Strengths Champion Certified Coach® and a certified Transformation Coach.

About: I am an Asa Griggs Candler Professor of Law at Emory University School of Law.  I rejoined the Emory faculty in 2016 after a decade at the University of Virginia School of Law, where I was most recently the Hardy Cross Dillard Professor of Law. For Fall 2022, I am the Hieken Visiting Professor in Patent Law at Harvard Law School.I served on both the National Academies Committee on Advancing Commercialization from the Federal Laboratories, and the National Academies Committee on University Management of Intellectual Property: Lessons from a Generation of Experience, Research, and Dialogue.  I am also an expert technical advisor to the African Union Commission in several World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) matters, served as the Friend of the Chair in the WIPO Intergovernmental Committee on Intellectual Property and Genetic Resources, Traditional Knowledge and Folklore from 2018-2022, and am a collaborator with the Harvard University Global Access in Action Program. I have served as a consultant to the UN Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD), the UN Food and Agriculture Organization Secretariat for the International Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture, and as a US Department of Commerce Commercial Law Development Program advisor.  In addition, I served as a member of the 2018 Ad Hoc Technical Expert Group on Digital Sequence Information on Genetic Resources for the CBD and Nagoya Protocol and have been an expert witness in several patent law disputes.  My scholarship focuses on comparative issues relating to patents and biotechnology, pharmaceuticals and access to medicines, traditional knowledge protection for indigenous peoples and local communities, technology transfer, and IP and social justice. In 2018, I was awarded and managed a $50,000 Emory Global Health Institute grant for a drug quality assurance program in Mozambique/Malawi, which involved a successful collaboration with the Harvard Global Access in Action (GAiA) program and the Emory-Rollins School of Public Health.I have published numerous articles and book chapters, as well as two books with co-authors: Bagley, Okediji and Erstling, International Patent Law & Policy (West Publishing 2013) and Patent Law in Global Perspective (Okediji and Bagley eds., Oxford University Press 2014).   A new book on International Patent Law is forthcoming with Professor Rochelle Dreyfuss (2022).  You can find much of my published work at:https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Margo-Bagleyand at https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/cf_dev/AbsByAuth.cfm?per_id=103398

About: Honson is the chairman of KPMG Asia Pacific and KPMG China. He also serves as a member of KPMG’s Global Board, Global Executive Committee and Global Investment Committee.He was elected chairman for the KPMG China firm in 2015. In 2017, he also became the chairman of KPMG's Asia Pacific region. Asia Pacific is one of the three major geographic regions in the KPMG network, with over 46,000 employees in 20 countries providing Audit, Tax and Advisory services. KPMG China is an integral part of the Asia Pacific region as well as KPMG’s global network.Honson began his career with KPMG in Canada in 1990 where he qualified as a Chartered Accountant and Chartered Business Valuator. He joined KPMG’s Hong Kong office in 1997 before moving to the Shanghai office in 2001, and later to the Beijing office in 2010. Honson has extensive experience serving inbound and outbound clients in the local and international markets and been responsible for advising on some of the largest cross-border transactions involving the China market. He has also led KPMG’s efforts in advising Chinese clients on their SOE reform initiatives as well as banking clients in dealing with non-performing loans in China.As the chairman of KPMG Asia Pacific and KPMG China, it is a priority for him to ensure the well-being of the firm’s people and foster an environment where they can develop their talents. He is dedicated to encouraging people in the firm to connect with and live by the KPMG Values – Integrity, Excellence, Courage, Together and For Better – and lead by example.Honson is a fellow of the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants, a member of the Institute of Chartered Professional Accountants of Ontario, Canada and a member of the Canadian Institute of Chartered Business Valuators.

About: Joy is the founder and director of 2020 Mom a non-profit closing gaps in maternal mental health care. Joy also served nearly 25 years working for Cigna, a fortune 50 health care company supporting quality improvement and regulatory compliance. Cigna provided her with substantial knowledge of healthcare operations and implementation of change nationally.  At Cigna, Joy specialized in quality improvement, innovation and compliance implementation and oversight and supported cross-functional teams in delivering outcomes. Joy has been recognized with several awards, including receiving the American Public Health Association's Maternal Child Health Advocate of the Year Award (2019), the federal government's Emerging Leader Award from Health and Human Services, Office of Women's Health (2016), Cigna's Volunteer of the Year award (2016), and the Junior League of Los Angeles' Founders cup (2012).She serves on several boards/committees, including California's Health and Human Services' Behavioral Health Task Force; Stanford University's California Maternal Quality Care Collaborative (CMQCC) Executive Committee/Board of Directors; The CMQCC Adverse Childhood Events in Maternal Health Task Force; the AMCHP/ASTHO PRISM project advisory board for improving maternal health; and she is an advisor on several Patient-Centered Outcomes Research Institute projects. 2020 Mom's brand/social change product portfolio includes 2020mom.org, TheBlueDotProject.org which focuses on the difficulties of motherhood and reducing stigma of anxiety/depression; and Mom-Congress.com, both a movement and a moment. The movement is membership-based, where the dream is Mom Congress will become similar to the Association of American Retired People (AARP) representing the voice of mothers on the hill.  The annual event brings together moms and those who support them in D.C. to hear from inspiring speakers and meet with Congress to address what matters most to moms.2020 Mom, convenes thought leaders and advocates to advance the diagnosis and treatment rates of women suffering from a maternal mental health disorders like postpartum depression. The non-profit is based in L.A. however the group's focus is on scalable, sustainable change, providing a platform for change, setting standards for insurers, hospitals and more. about_text: Joy is the founder and director of 2020 Mom a non-profit closing gaps in maternal mental health care. Joy also served nearly 25 years working for Cigna, a fortune 50 health care company supporting quality improvement and regulatory compliance. Cigna provided her with substantial knowledge of healthcare operations and implementation of change nationally. At Cigna, Joy specialized in quality improvement, innovation and compliance implementation and oversight and supported cross-functional teams in delivering outcomes. Joy has been recognized with several awards, including receiving the American Public Health Association's Maternal Child Health Advocate of the Year Award (2019), the federal government's Emerging Leader Award from Health and Human Services, Office of Women's Health (2016), Cigna's Volunteer of the Year award (2016), and the Junior League of Los Angeles' Founders cup (2012).She serves on several boards/committees, including California's Health and Human Services' Behavioral Health Task Force; Stanford University's California Maternal Quality Care Collaborative (CMQCC) Executive Committee/Board of Directors; The CMQCC Adverse Childhood Events in Maternal Health Task Force; the AMCHP/ASTHO PRISM project advisory board for improving maternal health; and she is an advisor on several Patient-Centered Outcomes Research Institute projects. 2020 Mom's brand/social change product portfolio includes 2020mom.org, TheBlueDotProject.org which focuses on the difficulties of motherhood and reducing stigma of anxiety/depression; and Mom-Congress.com, both a movement and a moment. The movement is membership-based, where the dream is Mom Congress will become similar to the Association of American Retired People (AARP) representing the voice of mothers on the hill. The annual event brings together moms and those who support them in D.C. to hear from inspiring speakers and meet with Congress to address what matters most to moms.2020 Mom, convenes thought leaders and advocates to advance the diagnosis and treatment rates of women suffering from a maternal mental health disorders like postpartum depression. The non-profit is based in L.A. however the group's focus is on scalable, sustainable change, providing a platform for change, setting standards for insurers, hospitals and more. About: Repeat founder on a mission to do good for the environment and startup community. I rapidly grew my last marketplace startup, Zwings, to 32 staff after winning multiple prized contracts that have since been extended. I am now using lessons learned how of how to scale a startup, fundraise and M&A to grow Foundy, an end-to-end online marketplace for startup acquisitions and investment. We are seamlessly connecting startups to acquirers as well as the latest resources and advisors to help founders achieve the highest exit valuation. We specialise in both partial and full buy outs because we recognise that many startups are still years away from a full exit but have shareholders that want to take some chips off the table by liquidating a fraction of their equity. A bit about my passion for Zwings and e-mobility:I grew up on 2 wheels by riding bikes and scooters from as early as I can remember. I founded Zwings from a source of deep-rooted passion for sustainable, convenient and data-driven shared transport. We emerged as one of the fastest growing British micromobility start ups through the depths of the pandemic by scaling from 1 to 32 staff in 9 months. We outcompeted much larger competitors to win exclusive contracts with cities to deploy e-scooter rental schemes in 6 cities/ towns and 2 universities. Our clients have since extended our contracts 3 consecutive times following the delivery of a good service. I then led the company through an M&A process involving multiple bidders.

About: I have worked in the office design, built environment, workplace and facilities management sectors for over 25 years as a marketing professional, consultant, editor and writer. At the start of 2013, I launched www.workplaceinsight.net, an online publication that explores the relationships between commercial interior design, workplace management, technology, human resources, the wider business world and society. In 2020, we launched IN Magazine, which is Europe's foremost publication exploring working lives, technology, flexible working and workplace management.In 2022, I launched Works magazine in partnership with Mick Jordan and Ben Capper. Works is set to become the leading dedicated workplace interiors title in the UK and Europe.I am a Director of And Places Ltd, the publishers of Work&Place, the world's leading journal looking at the many facets of the workplace.I was previously the launch editor of three of the UK's major print titles in the sector and have now applied my experience and knowledge of the built environment sector in developing content and communities through online media and events. Workplace Insight quickly became the UK's most widely read publication in its sector and the site continues to develop and grow. In addition I work with clients to develop their own online content, printed material and communities through social media, blogging, intellectual collateral and events. A fluent German speaker, I am also a Fellow of the Royal Society of the Arts.

Workplace: Partner, National Healthcare Practice at KPMG US
About: Advisory professional with over 25 years of experience in professional services, Karen has served in numerous roles in across both audit and consulting practices at KPMG. She joined the St. Louis office of KPMG in 1996 and was elected to the partnership in 2005. Karen served as the St. Louis Office Managing Partner from 2013 through 2020, and previously as the leader of the St. Louis Advisory Practice and led the Internal Audit, Risk and Compliance Services practice for the Gateway West and Northern Heartland business units. Healthcare Focus – National Consulting Industry LeaderKaren serves in KPMG’s National Healthcare Practice leveraging her experience with providers, payors and pharmacy benefit managers for the development of new solutions bringing value to our clients.  Karen has served as Lead Partner of some of the firm’s largest accounts and believes that when a relationship is based on an understanding of culture and expectations, we can more quickly meet a client’s business needs and bring greater value. Karen has led several leadership development initiatives for KPMG and in the St. Louis community, including the local KPMG Network of Women committee and various Employer of Choice initiatives. Named a “2014 Most Influential Business Woman” and one of the “7 Women to Watch in St. Louis” by the St. Louis Business Journal.

About: Born and raised on the outskirts of St. Louis, I am the Founder of Clayco, which I built from the ground up in St. Louis, MO in 1984. I invest most of my time in talent management, strategic planning, and making deals happen. I also served as the Commissioner General for the USA Pavilion at Expo 2020 Dubai, where I was the senior U.S. government representative and head of delegation to the event. 𝐁𝐮𝐬𝐢𝐧𝐞𝐬𝐬 𝐈𝐦𝐩𝐚𝐜𝐭• Clayco is ranked as one of the top firms for both design and construction in multiple categories by ENR, Midwest Real Estate News, and other publications.• We have been singled out for our sustainability practices and LEED building design (ENR Top Green Buildings 2020), our business best practices (SLCCC 2018), and as one of the best places to work (Crain’s Chicago 2018). • Clayco has set new standards for collaborative design, construction quality and craftsmanship, efficient project management, cost containment, and job site safety. 𝐂𝐨𝐦𝐦𝐮𝐧𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝐈𝐦𝐩𝐚𝐜𝐭• Support for medical research to improve outcomes and care for patients diagnosed with cancer or rare disease. Board of Trustees at the University of Chicago Medical Center, board member at the Central Institute for the Deaf, and member of the Scientific Advisory Council for the Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis. • Commitment to inclusion and diversity within the construction industry through ClaycoRising initiatives. • Appointment by Former President Barack Obama to the White House Preservation Committee.• Support for culture and the arts: Board of the St. Louis Symphony Orchestra, Director for the Chicago Architecture Biennial, and Business Council of the Art Institute of Chicago.

About: Tylik M. McMillan, a native of Lawrenceville Virginia, by way of Harrisburg Pennsylvania, is a proud HBCU  graduate of North Carolina Agricultural and Technical State University. Prior to his Project Management role at Gilead Sciences Inc. where he helped lead the company's Racial Equity Impact Fund (REIF) which supports high-impact organizations working to tackle racial inequities affecting Black communities across the country, he got his foundation at the National Action Network (NAN). Under the leadership and mentorship of Rev. Al Sharpton, Tylik served as a Washington D.C. Bureau Policy Advisor and National Director of Youth and College of NAN which is one of the nation's leading civil rights organizations working in the spirit and tradition of Dr. King, to promote the modern civil rights agenda. In his capacity, he worked to educate lawmakers and stakeholders on the challenges and opportunities facing Black communities, by advocating for more resources and policies that help invest and advance economic and social equality in communities. His government affairs portfolio includes issues from tech, policing/criminal justice, federal sentencing reform, ending racial profiling, equal employment protection, immigration, access to affordable/quality education, voting rights protection, housing, and other various issues that impact social and economic status, mobility and empowerment of urban and underserved communities. Tylik helped organize the 2020 Commitment March on Washington and 2021 March On for Voting Rights which drew over hundreds of thousands to Washington DC. Tylik is a member of Phi Beta Sigma Fraternity Inc. and serves on the Phi Beta Sigma, Sigma Political Action Committee Board of Directors. Tylik additionally serves as a member of the Association of Young Americans Board of Directors and member of the Virginia Civics Advisory Council. Alongside Reverend Al Sharpton, Tylik is a Thursday co-host of the nationally syndicated daily radio show Keepin’ It Real and a contributor to FoxSouls Black Report. Within his work Tylik has corresponded on MSNBC Weekends and was recognized as a 2020 Bloomberg 50 One to Watch, featured in the Washington Post, New York Times, Wall Street Journal, CNN, BBC World News, BET among other global, national, and local outlets. Tylik wishes to inspire other young people to get involved and make civic engagement the new norm, not the exception.

She also received an MBA from the Anderson School of Management with a dual degree focus in Marketing and Operations. Introduction: Full Name: Sarah Gosler | Workplace: Chief Operating Officer, Global Operations & Technology Office at BNY Mellon | Location: New York, New York, United States | Connections: 500+ | Photo: Yes
About: Sarah is the Chief Operating Officer for the Global Operations & Technology Office at BNY Mellon responsible for Leadership, Governance, Executive Reporting, Technical Thought Leadership, and People Experience. Before moving into Ops and Tech, she was the Global Head of Technology Marketing for BNYM. Previously, she was the Chief Marketing Officer for Wedbush Securities, a member of the Executive Management Committee and the Chief Marketing Officer of Lime Brokerage, a Wedbush affiliate. In her 18 years of experience, Sarah has created and managed 20 + leading brands and leveraged her vast expertise in Operations, Strategic Marketing, Communications, and Management Consulting to transform organizations. Prior to Wedbush, Sarah was the Head of Marketing for IFG Capital, a private equity firm with a portfolio of global companies including financial services, real estate development, and management consulting. Prior to IFG Capital, she was an executive consultant for start-ups and the Interim Executive Director for the Community Economics Lab (“CeLab”), where she advised entrepreneurs on creating and executing their branding initiatives. During her graduate program, Sarah worked for Sandia National Laboratories, a subsidiary of Lockheed Martin, and focused on transitioning the Tech organization into a business-centric operation. Sarah earned a BBA in Entrepreneurial Studies and Marketing, graduating Summa Cum Laude from the University of New Mexico. She also received an MBA from the Anderson School of Management with a dual degree focus in Marketing and Operations. Spanning her career, Sarah has received over 15 marketing awards, was honored as one of the Influential Business Women in Los Angeles in 2016, and named one of the “Women to Watch” by Direct Marketing News.

Client continuing implementation of the vision.•  $20 billion (assets) global refining and marketing company – 1 year after mega-merger, developed long-term strategy for integrated global downstream operations, initiated portfolio review of operating assets, and designed organizational construct for delivery of new business model (approximately 23,000 employees).  Migrated from full geographic model with siloed support functions to full functional model with shared services and regional Centers of Excellence.  Stated financial goal of $1 billion pre-tax benefits over 3 years. (NOTE: 5-year look-back indicates value creation of $1.3 billion).

About: With ~25+ years of experience, Sarah specializes in creating sustainable shareholder value through a variety of solutions including: strategy development and articulation, portfolio and customer profitability analysis, merger integration, performance management, organization/ business process optimization, and identification/ development of supporting technology solutions.The majority of Sarah's experience is with large-scale, global Energy, Chemicals and Industrial Products companies. Sarah is a trusted advisor and change agent with the ability to work across multiple stakeholders and drive business improvements across large matrix organizations. Migrated from full geographic model with siloed support functions to full functional model with shared services and regional Centers of Excellence. Stated financial goal of $1 billion pre-tax benefits over 3 years. (NOTE: 5-year look-back indicates value creation of $1.3 billion).

About: Ambi M G Parameswaran is a Brand Coach, Brand Strategist and Founder Brand-Building.com a Brand Advisory. In a career spanning 35+ years Ambi has handled assignments in marketing, sales and advertising with Rediffusion DY&R, Boots Company, UDI Yellow Pages and FCB Ulka Advertising. He has helped build numerous brands including Digene, Brufen, Santoor Soap, Sundrop Cooking Oil, TCS, ICICI Bank, Wipro, Indica Cars, Zee TV among others.He served as VP, then as CEO of FCB Ulka from 2003 to 2013. Ambi has been contributing articles to business publications, has conducted branding workshops for Indian/ MNC organizations and industry bodies like CII, FICCI, AIMA, OPPI etc.; he has spoken at TEDx and at the Kellogg India Summit at Northwestern University and Cornell University; he is a Adjunct Prof of Marketing at SPJIMR and a guest faculty at IIMC, IIMA, MICA and ISB. Ambi now has nine books to his credit including : â€œFCB-Ulka Brand Building Advertising â€“ Concepts and Cases I & II [with Kinjal Medh]â€; "Building Brand Value - Five Steps to Building Powerful Brandsâ€ (Winner of 2007 NTPC â€“ DMA Book Prize], "For God's Sake - An Adman on the Business of Religion", "Strategic Brand Management Indian Version" [with Prof K L Keller and Prof I Jacob]. He it the author of bestselling books "Nawabs Nudes Noodles - India Through 50 Years of Advertising" [a finalist at Crossword Popular Book Awards 2017], and "SPONGE- Leadership Lessons I Learnt From My Clients" [Fin Express #1 Bestseller]. In September 2020 he launched his tenth book, "SPRING- Bouncing Back From Rejection". Ambi served as the President of AAAI [2014-16] and President of Ad Club Bombay [2003â€“05]. He served on the Board of Governors of IIMC from 2007-2017; he is an independent director on the board of Galaxy Surfactants Ltd, THG Publishing Ltd, Qube Cinema Systems P Ltd, FDC Ltd [mrfs of Electral] and Rediff.com India Ltd. He received the Distinguished Alumnus Award from IITM in April 2009 and from IIMC in November 2018. He has a PhD from Mumbai University , an AMP from HBS and Executive Coaching Certification from CFI .

About: Dee Cohen Katz is the Managing Partner of Walsworth, overseeing operations in all three of the firm’s offices in Los Angeles, Orange County, and San Francisco. Walsworth is proud to have the largest California attorney presence of any certified Women's Business Enterprise (WBE) law firm in the country, in addition to being certified as women-owned by the California Public Utilities Commission. With more than twenty five years of experience, Dee also maintains an active litigation practice, handling matters throughout both Southern and Northern California and advising certain clients on a national basis. Her practice emphasizes the defense of claims involving general liability, toxic torts, business litigation, and products liability. She regularly represents manufacturers, distributors, retailers and premises/business owners.
